2. The facts of the case, in brief, are that ICB Islami Bank Limited, through its VIP Road Branch, filed Artha Rin Suit No.401 of 2015 before the 4th Artha Rin Adalat, Dhaka against the petitioners and others for realisation of loan amount of Tk.14,26,29,044.54 as on 05.05.2015 and other charges. In the said suit, the petitioners were impleaded as defendant Nos.1 and 2. The petitioners then filed written statement to contest the said suit. Thereafter, on 17.02.2016 the petitioners filed an application seeking stay of the said Aitha Rin Suit under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 ("the Ain"), on the ground that in respect of self same dispute between the petitioners and the bank the petitioners as plaintiffs filed Money Suit No.71 of 2009 against the ICR Islami Bank Limited, plaintiff bank, before the First Court of Joint District Judge, Dhaka seeking a decree for an amount of Tk.11,54,72,536/- and the said suit was contested by the bank as defendant: in the earlier suit by filing written statement and ultimately the said suit was decreed in part in favour of these petitioners vide judgment and decree dated 03.10.2013 declaring that the petitioners were entitled to get Tk.4,55,56,694/- from the bank. Against the said decree, both the petitioners and the bank preferred appeal, which are still pending before the High Court Division. That being so, it was claimed by the petitioners before the Adalat that, the Artha Rin Suit in question should be stayed. Upon such application, the Adalat, after hearing the parties, rejected the same vide order dated 29.03.2016 on the ground that, in view of the provisions under section 18(3) of the said Ain, there was no scope to stay proceedings of artha rin suit. Against the said Order, the petitioners moved the High Court Division and obtained the aforesaid Rule Nisi. At the time of issuance of the Rule Nisi, the High Court Division, vide ad-interim order dated 06.04.2016 stayed further proceedings of the said Artha Rin Suit No.401 of 2015 for a period of 6(six) months which was subsequently extended from time to time. 

 6. Mr. M. Qumrul Hoque Siddique, learned Advocate, appearing on behalf of the petitioners submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the admitted fact, i.e. the loan, the account, the parties, the claimed amount and issue of the Money Suit No.71 of 2009 is the same and the suit was decreed on contest and appeal preferred by both the parties are pending. Under these circumstances, over the same transaction, claim and issue the Artha Rin Suit No.401 of 2015 has been initiated as such the present suit is hopelessly barred by section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure which has occasioned failure of justice. He further submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate section 11 of the Code of Civil Procedure and on erroneous view discharged the Rule Nisi calls for interference by this Division. He lastly submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate the admitted facts and misinterpreted section 18(3) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 in discharging the Rule Nisi, as such the impugned judgment and order is liable to be set aside.
